Generate normalised 1-D convolution kernels (point-spread functions)

Source: R/convkernel.R
convkernel.Rd

Generates a numeric vector of length L that represents a point-spread function (PSF) or impulse-response kernel. The kernel is \(L^{1}\)-normalised (area = 1). Optionally it is shifted with shift_kernel so that a user-chosen percentile \(perc\) of the cumulative distribution falls on index \(1 + perc \cdot (L - 1)\); setting perc = 0 leaves the kernel unshifted. Alternatively, using perc = "mean" will move the centroid to the middle of the kernel.

The helper is useful for simulating blurred spike trains as observed in one-dimensional spectroscopy (GC-MS, NMR), calcium neuro-imaging, or epidemic curves where diagnosed cases are obtained by convolving infections with a delay-distribution kernel. Some of the available kernel families are:

  • Gaussian / Bigaussian / Exponentially Modified Gaussian (Gaussian * Exp) - common peak-shape models in gas-chromatography / mass-spectrometry.

  • Lorentzian - arises in 1-D NMR as the Fourier transform of an exponentially decaying free-induction decay (Cauchy-Lorentz distribution).

  • Exponential - standard calcium-indicator impulse response in neuro-imaging studies.

  • Gamma / Gamma * Exp - typical infection-to-diagnosis delay distributions in epidemiology and also sometimes used for chromatographic peak shapes.

All kernels returned by convkernel() integrate to 1 and are ready for use in convolution or deconvolution pipelines.

Usage

convkernel(
  type = c("gaussian", "bigaussian", "emg", "lorentzian", "laplace", "exponential",
    "gamma", "gammaexp"),
  L,
  params = list(),
  perc = NULL
)

shift_kernel(kernel, perc = "mean", method = c("linear", "integer"))

Arguments

type

One of `"gaussian"`, `"bigaussian"`, `"emg"` (exponentially modified Gaussian), `"lorentzian"` (Cauchy), `"laplace"` (two-sided exponential), `"exponential"` (one-sided exponential), `"gamma"`, `"gammaexp"` (convolution of Gamma with exponential).

L

Integer (>= 3). Kernel length.

params

Named list of shape parameters (see Details).

perc

Either `"mean"` (shift the centroid) or a numeric percentile in [0, 1].

kernel

Numeric vector - the PSF to be shifted.

method

`"linear"` (sub-sample interpolation) or `"integer"` (whole-sample shift).

Value

Numeric vector of length *L*.

shifted vector of the same length as `kernel`

Details

Default parameters for the different distributions are as follows:
gaussian: `sigma=2.5`
bigaussian: `sigma1=1`, `sigma2=5`
emg (gaussian * exponential):`sigma=2`,`tau=6 ` lorentzian: `gamma=2`
laplace: `tau=3`
exponential: `tau=3`
gamma: `k=9`, `tau=0.5`
gammaexp (gamma * exponential): `k=9` , ` tau_g=0.7` , `tau_e=0.7`

Returned vectors are **L^1-normalised**. If `align_percentile > 0` the kernel is shifted (by sub-sample interpolation) so that the requested percentile lies at its theoretical position inside the length-*L* vector.

See also

shift_kernel, convmatrix

Author

Tom Wenseleers tom.wenseleers@kuleuven.be \ Laboratory of Socioecology and Social Evolution, KU Leuven \ https://bio.kuleuven.be/eeb/tw/research \ ORCID: 0000-0002-1434-861X

Examples

## available convolution kernels
cols <- 1:8
k1 <- convkernel("gaussian",    51, list(sigma = 4))
k2 <- convkernel("bigaussian",  51, list(sigma1 = 2, sigma2 = 6))
k3 <- convkernel("emg",         51, list(sigma = 2, tau = 6))
k4 <- convkernel("lorentzian",  51, list(gamma = 3))
k5 <- convkernel("laplace",     51, list(tau = 4))
k6 <- convkernel("exponential", 51, list(tau = 5))
k7 <- convkernel("gamma",       51, list(k = 9, tau = 0.5))
k8 <- convkernel("gammaexp",    51, list(k = 9, tau_g = 0.7, tau_e = 0.7))
matplot(cbind(k1,k2,k3,k4,k5,k6,k7,k8), type = "l", lty = 1, col = cols,
        xlab = "kernel index", ylab = "density",
        main = "Convolution kernels\n(point-spread functions)")
legend("topright",
       legend = c("Gaussian", "Bigaussian", "EMG", "Lorentzian",
                  "Laplace", "Exponential", "Gamma", "Gammaexp"),
       lty = 1, cex = 0.8, y.intersp = 0.8,
       col = cols, bty = "n")

## peak broadening as observed at higher concentrations in GC/MS analysis
cols=1:3
matplot(cbind(
  convkernel("bigaussian", 51,
             list(sigma1 = 2, sigma2 = 4), perc = 0.001),
  convkernel("bigaussian", 51,
             list(sigma1 = 2*2, sigma2 = 4*2), perc = 0.001),
  convkernel("bigaussian", 51,
             list(sigma1 = 2*3, sigma2 = 4*3), perc = 0.001)), 
  xlab = "kernel index", ylab = "density",
  main = paste("Bigaussian point spread functions",
               "(sigma1 = 2, 4, 6; sigma2 = 2 * sigma1)",
               "perc = 0.001",
               sep = "\n"),
  col = cols, lty = 1,
  type="l")
